name: Margarita Bermejo Cano
headline: People Science & Analytics
specialisms: AI Adoption · Customer & Product Insights · Workforce Measurement
summary: People science and analytics professional with 15+ years across HR, workforce and customer analytics, now focused on employee experience and AI adoption. At Microsoft, I lead analytical work on AI readiness and agentic ways of working; previously, I delivered customer-facing people analytics at LinkedIn Glint and regional workforce insights at MetLife. I combine psychometric validation, predictive and mixed-methods analysis with practical recommendations and reusable workflows in R, SQL and Python.

projects.title: Readiness for agentic ways of working.
projects.summary: Lead analyst on enterprise research into agentic AI readiness and adoption.
projects.question: What evidence helps organisations understand readiness for and adoption of agentic ways of working?
projects.contribution: Led the analytical work across an in-depth report series, using exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, regression, comparative analysis and descriptive methods.
projects.outcome: Delivered an internal research evidence base for decisions about agentic readiness and adoption.

projects.title: Measurement before interpretation.
projects.summary: Analytical leadership on AI readiness measurement and the factors associated with it.
projects.question: Are we measuring organisational AI readiness reliably, and what factors are associated with it?
projects.contribution: Tested the instrument's structure and reliability using EFA, CFA and item analysis; examined factors associated with readiness using regression, correlation and relative weight analysis.
projects.outcome: Produced validated measurement and analysis referenced in a published eBook on AI readiness and employee experience.

projects.title: Listening to early AI adopters.
projects.summary: From the first findings report to a sustained enterprise AI survey-reporting cycle.
projects.question: What do early users tell us about adopting an enterprise AI assistant?
projects.contribution: Co-produced the first findings report as one of two analysts, then owned recurring reporting. Partnered with digital-experience and future-of-work researchers.
projects.outcome: Findings featured in a public workplace-research report and were cited at the company's annual conference. Maintained recurring and quarterly reporting for the early-access programme.

projects.title: Listening after a product migration.
projects.summary: Sole analyst on a mixed-methods study of the customer experience after migration.
projects.question: How did customers experience the migration, and which themes should product teams prioritise?
projects.contribution: Combined quantitative survey analysis with thematic coding of open-text responses, distinguishing recurring themes from individual observations.
projects.outcome: Translated customer feedback into prioritised, actionable recommendations for the teams responsible for the experience.

projects.title: Improving a recommended-action library.
projects.summary: End-to-end content-library ownership spanning architecture, quality and supplier-content decisions.
projects.question: How can a recommended-action library remain useful, reliable and worth its licensing cost?
projects.contribution: Redesigned its information architecture, remediated 70+ broken or outdated links and evaluated licensed content against performance evidence.
projects.outcome: Retired underperforming content and reduced annual licensing spend while improving the reliability of the library.

projects.title: A recurring content insights review.
projects.summary: A recurring content insights review adopted by two teams, including product.
projects.question: How can fragmented content-performance signals become a useful, shared view?
projects.contribution: Designed and authored a recurring review, consolidating evidence from multiple sources into an accessible narrative for people science and product stakeholders.
projects.outcome: Two teams adopted it as a standing review artefact, giving stakeholders a consistent basis for discussing content performance.

projects.title: Agreeing the right data foundation.
projects.summary: A cross-functional assessment of options for unified licence and usage data.
projects.question: Should teams build a new dataset or use an existing source to answer a shared business question?
projects.contribution: Defined the access problem and assessed options against speed, scalability, complexity and compliance. Worked with engineering, product and privacy partners to align on an approach.
projects.outcome: Established an agreed approach and documented the trade-offs for the next phase of work.

projects.title: A better starting point for analysis.

projects.outcome: Created a documented, reusable method for structuring analytical planning.

projects.title: Refreshing learning resources and action plans.

projects.contribution: Sourced 145 learning video resources, revised 47 action plans and cleared obsolete references from 112 plans.
